method.hurt: A game counts when the player's NFL team played, he took no snap, and he was on injured reserve, PUP or NFI, listed Out or Doubtful on the official injury report, or listed Questionable and then inactive. Byes, healthy scratches, suspensions and unsigned players never count.
method.owner: Each missed game is charged to whoever had the player on their Yahoo roster that week, so a traded player bills the team that holds him that week: games he missed before a trade stay with the old team, games after it go to the new one. A player cut because he got hurt keeps billing the team that cut him while he stays hurt and unclaimed, because losing him was the injury.
method.bill: The Injury Bill is starter points left on the table. Each week we build the best lineup a team could have set with its hurt players available, at their healthy average, and the best lineup it could set without them, with everyone else at Yahoo's projection for that week. The gap is the bill. A hurt player who would have been on the bench anyway costs nothing; a hurt stud who forces a waiver body into the lineup costs the difference. When several players are out the same week, the gap is split by how much each one alone would have added.
method.dollars: Dead money is the draft-capital view: what the player cost the team holding him (auction price if drafted or traded for, FAAB bid if claimed off waivers) times the games he missed.
method.points: Everything runs on projections, never on what happened later. A hurt player is valued at his preseason projection under this league's scoring, blended 50/50 with Yahoo's weekly projection for him once he has three active weeks; a pickup nobody projected uses Yahoo's weekly projections alone. Everyone else is valued at Yahoo's projection for that week. The ward's cost for next week uses the same projected values for the whole roster.
method.source: Injury reports, NFL roster status and snap counts from nflverse. Rosters from the league's Yahoo box scores. Draft prices from the 2026 auction.
